# Aha — Employee Rewards Programme

## What is Aha?
Aha is the employee-facing rewards and recognition platform. Points are
earned through business-aligned actions and can be redeemed for vouchers,
merchandise and experiences on the Aha portal.

## Earning Points
| Trigger | Points |
|---|---|
| Successful employee referral hired | 5,000 |
| Cross-sell win (per qualifying win) | 250 |
| Audit-clean month (branch or ops team) | 500 |
| CSAT topping the region | 1,500 |
| Certification pass (approved list) | 2,000 |

## Redemption
- Minimum redemption balance: 1,000 points.
- Points expire 24 months after being awarded.
- Redemption catalogue: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra vouchers, curated experiences,
  branded merchandise.

## Anti-Abuse Controls
- Referrals that leave within 6 months are clawed back automatically.
- Fake cross-sell entries are flagged during quarterly audit and lead to
  point reversal and disciplinary action.

## Support
For Aha portal issues, raise a ticket via HResponse under `Aha > Portal`.
For point disputes, use `Aha > Point Reversal`.

# Axis Phone — Callback Workflow

## What is Axis Phone?
Axis Phone is the assisted-service channel where relationship managers and
contact-centre agents can be requested to call the customer back at a chosen
slot.

## Requesting a Callback (customer path)
1. Customer selects `Axis Phone` in the assistant or on the mobile app.
2. Provides preferred slot (30-minute windows between 09:00 and 20:00 IST).
3. Provides callback number (defaults to the number on file).
4. Selects the topic — `Account queries`, `Loan advisory`, `Cards`,
   `Wealth advisory`, `Complaint`, `Other`.
5. Receives an SMS confirmation with the callback reference ID.

## Assignment
The workflow engine picks an agent by:
- Topic → queue mapping.
- Customer segment (Retail / Priority / Burgundy).
- Language preference (English / Hindi / Regional).
- Agent load balancing — least-active-eligible agent wins.

## SLA
- Priority / Burgundy: **within 15 minutes** of the requested slot.
- Retail: **within 60 minutes**.
- Missed callbacks trigger an auto retry once and are flagged for supervisor
  review.

## Post-Call
- Agent must dispose the call with a valid outcome code and add the call
  summary in the CRM.
- CSAT survey SMS goes out within 30 minutes of call disposition.

## Reference
`AP-CB-2026-01` · Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Change Management (CR) — Standard Process

## Change Categories
| Category | Definition | Approval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | Pre-approved template, low risk | Team Lead |
| Normal | Business change with a defined blast radius | CAB |
| Emergency | Production incident fix within 24 hours | Emergency CAB |

## Required Artefacts
Every CR must attach:
1. Business justification and scope.
2. Impact assessment (customer facing? cross-team? regulator? data-migration?).
3. Roll-out plan with owners.
4. Roll-back plan verified in the last drill.
5. Test evidence — unit, integration, UAT.
6. Communication plan (mailer templates, banner text).

- Standing CAB every **Tuesday and Thursday, 16:00 IST**.
- Cut-off for CR submission is 24 hours before CAB.
- Emergency CRs are triaged on demand via the emergency channel.

## Blackout Windows
No non-emergency production changes during:
- Financial year-end (last 5 business days of March).
- Half-year close (last 3 business days of September).
- RBI mandated reporting windows.

`CR-STD-2026-01` · Owner: Change Advisory Board.

A **Change Request** is any planned addition, modification or removal of a
production or production-adjacent component that could affect service
availability, integrity or compliance.

- Business justification.
- Impact assessment (services, users, data).
- Roll-back plan with owner and time budget.
- Test evidence (unit, integration, UAT sign-off).
- Communication plan.
- Downtime window (if any).

No production CRs during:
- Financial year-end close (last week of March, first week of April).
- Half-yearly close (last week of September, first week of October).
- Regulatory reporting window (2 business days before submission deadline).

|---|---|

# Fixed Deposits — Product Note

## Product Variants
- **Regular FD:** interest paid monthly / quarterly / on maturity.
- **Reinvestment FD:** compounded quarterly, single maturity payout.
- **Tax Saver FD:** 5-year lock-in, deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5L.
- **Senior Citizen FD:** additional 0.50% over the applicable card rate.
- **NRE / NRO FD:** available to NRIs subject to source-of-fund controls.

## Booking Channels
- Internet banking (retail).
- Mobile app.
- Any branch during business hours.
- Relationship manager for HNI customers.

## Premature Withdrawal
- Allowed on all variants except the 5-year Tax Saver FD.
- Penalty: 1.00% below the applicable card rate for the period run OR the
  booking rate, whichever is lower.
- Sweep-in FDs are broken in FIFO order to fund the linked savings account.

## Nomination
Nomination is mandatory. It can be captured at booking or updated later via
the branch or internet banking. Joint holdings must specify the operating
mandate (either or survivor / former or survivor / joint).

## Auto Renewal
Auto renewal defaults to `Reinvestment` at the prevailing rate for the same
tenure. Customers can switch this off during booking.

`FA-FD-2026-01` · Owner: Liabilities product team.

# Mutual Funds — Advisor Playbook

## Product Suite
Axis Wealth offers execution-only and advisory access across the following
mutual fund categories:
- Equity: large-cap, flexi-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, ELSS, sector/thematic.
- Debt: liquid, ultra-short, money market, corporate bond, gilt, credit risk.
- Hybrid: aggressive, conservative, balanced advantage, multi-asset.
- International feeder funds (currency hedged and unhedged).

## Suitability Framework
An advisor must complete the customer's risk profile before recommending any
scheme:
1. Risk tolerance questionnaire (12 questions).
2. Time horizon and liquidity check.
3. KYC + FATCA declaration.
Recommendations must map to the resulting risk band (Conservative / Moderate
/ Aggressive). Deviations require written justification and a customer
consent letter.

## SIP Rules
- Minimum SIP: ₹500/month (except direct-plan schemes; check factsheet).
- SIP registration cut-off: 8 days before first debit date.
- Pause / cancel SIP: T-2 working days before the debit date.
- Skipping instalments is allowed up to 3 months in a rolling year without
  breaking the mandate.

## Exit Load Ready-Reckoner
- Equity funds: 1% if redeemed within 12 months of allocation, nil after.
- Liquid funds: graded exit load from day 1 to day 7 as per SEBI norms.
- ELSS: statutory 3-year lock-in — no early exit permitted.

## Advisor Do & Don'ts
Do: disclose commission, provide TER details, share KIM before purchase.
Don't: guarantee returns, make comparisons with fixed deposits without a
disclaimer, or process transactions without a signed suitability report.

## Reference
`FA-MF-2026-01` · Owner: Wealth Advisory desk.

text:
# Background: Know Your Customer (KYC)

Know Your Customer (KYC) is the collection of laws, regulations and guidelines
that require regulated financial businesses to verify the identity, suitability
and risks associated with maintaining a business relationship with a customer.
These procedures fit within the broader scope of Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
and Counter-Terrorism Financing (CTF) regulations.

Modern KYC frameworks are built on three pillars:

- **Customer Identification Program (CIP)** — legally mandated verification of
  any person or entity opening a new account, including name, date of birth,
  address and a government-issued identification number.
- **Customer Due Diligence (CDD)** — understanding the nature and purpose of a
  client relationship, developing a risk profile, and ongoing monitoring of
  transactions for suspicious activity.
- **Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)** — extra checks for higher risk clients such
  as politically exposed persons (PEPs), cross-border correspondent banking
  relationships, or businesses operating in jurisdictions with strategic
  deficiencies in their AML/CFT regimes.

Regulated entities are required to maintain a written, risk-based KYC program
that: forms a reasonable belief that they know the true identity of every
customer; verifies identity within a reasonable time; checks the customer
against sanctions and terror watchlists; and retains records for a defined
period after account closure (typically five years).

Electronic KYC (eKYC) uses digital identity verification, biometric checks and
liveness detection to onboard customers remotely. In India, the Reserve Bank of
India first issued KYC guidelines for banks in 2002; video KYC (V-CIP) is
permitted for eligible savings account onboarding, subject to procedural
controls around live capture, random challenge and geo-tagging.

_Source: Adapted from Wikipedia's "Know your customer" article,
Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0._

metadata.title: Kyc Background

text:
# Background: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large
language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from
external data sources at inference time, instead of relying solely on their
pre-training data.

At a high level, a RAG system operates in three stages:

1. **Indexing.** External data (documents, tables, knowledge graphs) is
   converted into vector embeddings and stored in a vector database.
2. **Retrieval.** For a given user query, a retriever selects the most
   relevant documents from the vector store. Reranking, hybrid search
   (sparse + dense) and late-interaction models such as ColBERT are common
   accuracy improvements.
3. **Generation.** The retrieved passages are supplied to the LLM through
   prompt engineering ("prompt stuffing"), so the model prioritises the
   retrieved context over its parametric memory when producing an answer.

RAG improves factuality, allows citing sources for verification, and removes
the need to retrain the base model when knowledge changes. It does not
eliminate hallucinations: models can still misinterpret retrieved context,
combine outdated and updated information, or generate false claims when
retrieval quality is poor ("RAG poisoning"). Robust RAG systems therefore
depend heavily on chunking strategy, retriever quality, reranking, and
downstream guardrails.

_Source: Adapted from Wikipedia's "Retrieval-augmented generation" article,
Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0._

metadata.title: Rag Background

# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

# Re-Hiring Policy

## Purpose
This policy defines the criteria under which former employees ("alumni") may be
considered for rehire into Axis Bank.

## Eligibility
An alumnus may be considered for re-hire if all of the following are true:
1. The employee resigned or superannuated from Axis Bank in good standing.
2. There was no adverse audit or disciplinary finding at the time of exit.
3. A cooling period of at least 12 months has elapsed since the exit date.
4. The role being considered is at or below the last held grade at the bank.

## Non-Eligibility
An alumnus is NOT eligible for re-hire if any of the following are true:
- Exit was due to a "termination for cause" or breach of code of conduct.
- The employee is currently under a signed non-solicitation clause with a
  competitor and the clause is unexpired.
- Alumnus was identified as a "Do Not Rehire" during exit interviews.

## Approval Workflow
Every re-hire must be signed off by:
- HR Business Partner for the hiring unit.
- Business head at N-1 to CEO.
- Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO).

## Compensation
- Compensation for rehires is decided based on the target role and market band.
- Prior tenure is counted only for:
  - Gratuity computation.
  - Long-service awards.
- Prior tenure does NOT confer any accrued privileged leave or accumulated PF.

## Exceptions
Exceptions must be endorsed by the CEO and are limited to strategic hires
(business heads, technology leadership, key regulatory roles).

## References
- Policy code: HR-REHIRE-2026-01
- Last reviewed: March 2026
- Owner: HR Business Policy team

# Network Troubleshooting Playbook

## Wi-Fi / LAN Not Working
1. Check the physical cable / dock is seated firmly.
2. `Windows key + I → Network & Internet → Advanced → Network reset`.
3. Try a different port or the guest wifi to isolate infra vs. laptop.
4. If still failing, open Unidesk under `IT Helpdesk > Connectivity > Wired/Wireless`.

## VPN Disconnect Loop
- Confirm you are on the corporate VPN group in Anyconnect (not the guest
  group).
- Toggle **Airplane mode** for 10 seconds to refresh the network stack.
- Clear the VPN posture cache (`%ProgramData%\Cisco\AnyConnect\posture\ISEPosture.cfg`) and re-launch.
- If disconnects persist within 60 seconds of connect, log a P2 SR — likely
  a certificate issue.

## Slow Application Load
Order of triage:
1. Ping the app endpoint from a command prompt; RTT > 200ms indicates
   backbone congestion.
2. Check `Task Manager > Performance` — is disk I/O at 100%? Might be a
   background AV scan.
3. Check DNS — `nslookup finacle.internal` should return a 10.x address.
4. Clear browser cache & retry.

## Escalation Matrix
| Priority | Definition | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Full site / branch down | 15 min response |
| P2 | Individual user, business-critical app | 2 hrs |
| P3 | Individual user, non-critical | Next business day |
| P4 | Enhancement / how-to | 3 business days |

## Reference
`IT-NET-2026-01` · Owner: Network Operations.

# Anti-Money Laundering (AML) — Operating Framework

## Purpose
The AML framework prevents the bank's channels being used to launder proceeds
of crime and to finance terrorism, in line with the Prevention of Money
Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 and RBI Master Direction on KYC.

## Three Lines of Defence
- **1st line — Business units:** onboard customers correctly, monitor
  transactions, escalate red flags.
- **2nd line — Financial Crime Compliance (FCC):** owns the AML policy,
  runs the sanctions and PEP screening tools, files STRs.
- **3rd line — Internal Audit:** independently tests the framework annually.

## Customer Risk Categorisation
- **Low risk:** salaried resident individuals with no adverse hits.
- **Medium risk:** self-employed, high-net-worth individuals, non-resident
  individuals with low transaction velocity.
- **High risk:** NGOs, cash-intensive businesses, PEPs, customers in
  FATF-listed jurisdictions.

Risk category drives periodic KYC refresh frequency (see the KYC standard).

## Reporting Obligations
| Report | Threshold | Filing SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cash Transaction Report (CTR) | Cash > ₹10L / day per customer | 15th of the following month |
| Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) | On red flag | 7 working days from detection |
| Counterfeit Currency Report (CCR) | Any incident | 7 working days |
| Cross-Border Wire Transfer Report (CBWTR) | > ₹5L | 15th of the following month |

## Training
All customer-facing staff must complete the annual AML e-learning by
30 September of each year. Non-completion is tracked as an audit finding.

## Reference
`LAW-AML-2026-02` · Owner: Financial Crime Compliance unit.

metadata.title: Aml Framework

# Data Privacy — DPDP Act 2023 Alignment

## What the DPDP Act Requires
The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 defines how personal
data of Indian citizens ("Data Principals") must be processed by any entity
("Data Fiduciary"). Axis Bank is a Significant Data Fiduciary and follows the
obligations below.

## Lawful Grounds for Processing
Bank processes personal data only on one of the following grounds:
- Explicit consent obtained through the customer journey.
- Legitimate use for the performance of a service the customer has requested.
- Compliance with applicable laws (RBI Master Directions, PMLA, income tax
  reporting).
- Employment obligations for staff data.

## Data Principal Rights
Customers can raise these requests through the customer portal or by writing
to `dpo@axisbank.com`:
- Right to information about processing.
- Right to correction of inaccurate data.
- Right to erasure (subject to statutory retention).
- Right to grievance redressal (30 day SLA).
- Right to nominate a person to exercise their rights.

## Retention
Customer KYC and transaction data are retained for a **minimum of 8 years**
after account closure per PMLA. Beyond that, data is anonymised or purged
unless a legal hold is in effect.

## Data Breach Handling
Any suspected breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours by raising
a `Priority-Zero` incident on Unidesk. The DPO reports notifiable breaches to
the Data Protection Board within 72 hours.

## Reference
`LAW-DPDP-2026-01` · Owner: Data Protection Office (DPO).

metadata.title: Data Privacy Dpdp

# Know Your Customer (KYC) Standard

## Purpose
This standard defines the mandatory identity and address verification a
banker must perform before onboarding any customer, in line with the RBI
Master Direction on KYC.

## Acceptable Officially Valid Documents (OVDs)
- Aadhaar (with masked number, per UIDAI guideline).
- PAN.
- Passport.
- Driving licence issued by an RTO.
- Voter ID issued by ECI.
- Job card issued by NREGA duly signed by the state government.

## Video KYC (V-CIP)
V-CIP is available for eligible savings account onboarding subject to:
- Genuine live video with the customer visible from mid-torso up.
- Random challenge (e.g., "Show your OVD now").
- Officer capturing at least 3 still frames during the call.
- Geo-tagging of the customer's location.

## Periodic Update Frequency
| Risk Category | Frequency |
|---|---|
| High risk | Every 2 years |
| Medium risk | Every 8 years |
| Low risk | Every 10 years |

## Deficient KYC
Accounts flagged with deficient KYC are moved to `PARTIAL FREEZE` after
two written reminders. All debits (excluding regulatory / statutory dues)
are blocked in this state.

## References
- Policy code: LAW-KYC-2026-01
- Aligned to RBI Master Direction on KYC (as amended).
- Owner: Compliance — Financial Crime unit.
